To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a recombinant cytomegaloviral vaccine expressing the high-affinitity NKG2D-ligand RAE- 1γ is attenuated, elicits long-lasting protective immunity, and is stable during infection.
a recombinant MCMV expressing RAE-1 γ is attenuated in vivo, and induces long lasting protective immunity against a lethal challenge with MCMV.

(1) RAE-1MCMV is attenuated in vivo and elicits long-lasting protective immunity; (2) RAE- 1MCMV infection is efficiently controlled by immunocompromised hosts; (3) maternal RAE-1 MCMV immunization protects neonatal mice from infection; (4) the RAE- 19 gene does not exhibit sequence variation during infection.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing novel strategies to control cytomegaloviruses (CMVs), which cause serious disease in immunocompromised hosts, including transplant recipients.
the immune control of mouse CMV (MCMV) infection.
the development of a vaccine against human cytomegaloviruses (CMVs).

a recombinant cytomegaloviral vector expressing an activating NK cell ligand is a promising vaccine candidate.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a virus expressing the high affinity ligand for an NK cell receptor is attenuated, and that this attenuation is associated with improved vaccine properties, including the generation of long-lasting immunity and the induction of maternal antibody transfer.
we engineered a virus expressing a ligand that binds an immune receptor, and this virus was attenuated and immunogenic in vivo.
we have engineered a recombinantly attenuated mouse cytomegallovirus that elicits protective immune responses against a lethal challenge of the virus, but is not able to escape immune surveillance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of a recomblinant virus encoding the ligands for an activating NK receptor could be an important approach to developing a HCMV vaccine that is both safe and effective.
we engineered a mouse cytomegallovirus (MCMV) that expresses the ligand for the NK cell receptor NKG2D, which is a potent activating NK cell receptor.
a virus that expresses a high affinity NKG2D agonist ligand, RAE- 1γ, is attenuated in vivo and elicits a robust protective immune response in mice.
